findings.title: Accidental debugging change reduces global cleanup job interval from 10m to 1m
findings.body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This runs all background cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, and query history) every minute instead of every 10 minutes, with a 9-minute timeout per run. This appears to be a leftover from local testing and will significantly increase background database and filesystem load.

findings.title: Leftover `r.log.Error` debugging logs in annotation cleanup
findings.body: In `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, and 579), `r.log.Error` is called unconditionally on every batch iteration, even when `err` is `nil`, and dumps the entire slice of `ids` (which can be thousands of IDs per batch). This will flood error logs and alerting systems during normal cleanup runs. These should be removed or changed to `Debug` level without logging the full `ids` slice.

findings.title: O(N^2) string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE query
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs` (lines 609-612), when `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999` on SQLite, the ID list string is built in a loop using `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. Because strings in Go are immutable, this copies the entire accumulated string on each iteration, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and time (e.g. for the 32,767 batch size in the test, this allocates gigabytes of memory). Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` instead.

findings.title: PostgreSQL and MySQL parameter limits are not handled when `ids` is large
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, only SQLite's parameter limit (999) is bypassed by inlining integer IDs or chunking; for other databases, `len(ids)` placeholders (`?`) are generated in a single `DELETE FROM ... WHERE id IN (...)` statement. Both PostgreSQL and MySQL have prepared-statement parameter limits of 65,535 (`uint16`). If `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is configured above 65,535 (or even large enough in general), `session.Exec` will fail on PostgreSQL and MySQL. Since `ids` is a `[]int64`, formatting the integers directly (with a `strings.Builder`) or chunking the `DELETE` statement across all dialects avoids parameter limit failures on all databases.
